test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 03 Aug, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Some of them available to legal expertise.
Some of them are available to foreigners.
The Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Constitution does not provide for their direct enforcement.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental duties** are a set of moral obligations that are mentioned in the **Indian Constitution**, which every citizen is expected to follow.
 
• These duties are **not directly** enforceable by law, but they serve as a reminder to **citizens to be responsible** and **patriotic** towards their country.
 
• **Reasonable restrictions** can be imposed on these duties if they clash with other fundamental rights or public interests.
 
• None of these duties are available to **legal expertise or foreigners**, they are only applicable to Indian citizens.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution through the **42nd Amendment in 1976.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• List of **11 fundamental duties:**

 
 
• Respect the **national flag and anthem**, and abide by the constitution.
 
• Adhere to the **freedom struggle's** ideals.
 
• Preserve India's **integrity and sovereignty**.
 
• When called upon, **defend **the nation and perform national duties.
 
• Fostering a sense of **shared fraternity.**
 
• Preserve the nation's **diverse culture.**
 
• Keep the surroundings** natural.**
 
• Develop a** kind and scientific temperament.**
 
• Keep** public property safe** and abstain from **violence.**
 
• Aim for **greatness** in every aspect of your life.
 
• It is the responsibility of all parents and guardians to send their children, aged** 6 to 14, to school. **
